title: Xanthe and the House
premise: Isandro Voss, a rationalist property surveyor, is hired to appraise the decaying Aldermere House days before the harvest moon, only to discover the house appraises back—its rooms shifting, its photographs multiplying a chair that was never there. As she documents impossible measurements, Isandro uncovers the truth: her grandmother, decades ago, invited something in to save her dying family, and the debt has come due with interest. To survive until sunrise, Isandro must choose between completing the appraisal that would transfer the house's hunger to new owners or offering herself as payment. In the end, she breaks the contract by refusing both duty and survival at any price—and walks out at dawn carrying the house's memory inside her, forever changed but free.
about_author: Ulyana Hartwell is the pen name of a former rural land assessor who spent years cataloguing properties no one wanted to enter twice. She writes horror from a farmhouse she insists is perfectly ordinary.

chapters.title: The Commission
chapters.summary: Third-person limited on Isandro. She accepts an unusually generous appraisal job for Aldermere House from a lawyer who won't meet in person. Her skepticism is established through dry professional ritual. Emotional beat: confident detachment masking loneliness after her grandmother's funeral.

chapters.title: Measurements That Don't Hold
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. First walkthrough: rooms measure differently on second pass; a hallway is four feet longer than it should be. She blames old construction and settling foundations. Emotional beat: irritation hardening into denial.

chapters.title: The Extra Chair
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Reviewing her grandmother's photo albums for provenance research, she finds every family photograph now includes a high-backed chair against the wall—a chair absent from her childhood memories. Emotional beat: first cold finger of dread.

chapters.title: Dust and Deeds
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. In the county archive she finds the deed chain broken in 1963—the year her grandmother married. The previous owner's file contains a surveyor's notes ending mid-sentence. Emotional beat: curiosity outpacing caution.

chapters.title: What the Camera Saw
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Her own site photos show the chair in Aldermere's parlor, though she photographed an empty room. Zooming in, she sees an impression in the cushion, fresh. Emotional beat: denial cracking.

chapters.title: Neighbor at the Fence Line
chapters.summary: POV shifts to Marisol Quist, elderly neighbor. She warns Isandro not to stay past dark and mentions 'the year of the harvest moon' before catching herself. Emotional beat: fear passed like an inheritance.

chapters.title: Overnight by Necessity
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. A storm closes the road; she decides to sleep in the house rather than abandon expensive equipment. Rationalization as self-betrayal. Emotional beat: pride making a bad bargain.

chapters.title: Footsteps Above
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. At 3 a.m., measured footsteps cross the floor above—there is no finished upstairs. She finds dustless footprints leading to a sealed door. Emotional beat: terror managed like a work problem, badly.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Letters
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. In the sealed room, a box of letters: her grandmother writing to someone called 'the Tenant,' pleading for more time, promising 'the next one.' Emotional beat: love curdling into betrayal.

chapters.title: The Appraisal That Fights Back
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Her report software corrupts itself; printed pages rearrange values. The house wants to be appraised—wants a valuation declared. Emotional beat: understanding she's participating in something.

chapters.title: Marisol's Story, Part One
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV, 1963 flashback. Young Marisol watches her friend Ellery Voss—Isandro's grandmother—desperate over a dying husband, visit a man who speaks for the house. Emotional beat: pity shadowed by complicity.

chapters.title: Marisol's Story, Part Two
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. The bargain: the house heals what it's told, in exchange for a keeper who stays 'until the moon forgets.' Ellery signs, believing she can leave anytime. Emotional beat: hope as the cruelest currency.

chapters.title: Return to the House
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Armed with the letters' context, she returns intending only to finish and leave. The front door is where the parlor used to be. Emotional beat: control slipping.

chapters.title: Rooms With Opinions
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The house rearranges to keep her: stairs lengthen, exits become walls, the chair appears in every room she enters. Emotional beat: claustrophobic rage.

chapters.title: The Tenant Speaks
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. A voice through the walls—not menacing, almost weary—offers to explain the terms if she sits in the chair. She refuses. Emotional beat: defiance as identity.

chapters.title: What Was Invited In
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. She finds the original invitation document: her grandmother's signature binding 'all who carry her blood.' Isandro realizes she inherited the contract, not just the house. Emotional beat: grief weaponized against her.

chapters.title: Sunrise Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Marisol calls: the harvest moon rises tomorrow night; contracts settle at moonrise, not midnight. Isandro has one day. Emotional beat: countdown pressure.

chapters.title: The Lawyer's Client
chapters.summary: POV of Mr. Corben, the lawyer. He represents an investment consortium that has bought and sold Aldermere eleven times; each owner died or vanished, each sale required a fresh appraisal. Emotional beat: banal evil, profit without malice.

chapters.title: A Fair Market Value
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Corben offers her a way out: complete the appraisal naming a buyer, and the debt transfers. He genuinely believes this is kindness. Emotional beat: temptation dressed as professionalism.

chapters.title: Photographs of the Living
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. New photos appear: her coworkers, her estranged brother Daniel—all seated near the chair. The house shows her what it can reach. Emotional beat: protective panic.

chapters.title: Calling Daniel
chapters.summary: Daniel's POV. Isandro calls her brother after two years of silence; he hears fear under her flat voice and drives toward her despite their history. Emotional beat: love persisting through damage.

chapters.title: The Chair Remembers
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. She finally sits—not accepting, but interrogating. Visions flood: every keeper, every harvest moon, her grandmother aging in fast-forward as the house drank years. Emotional beat: horrified empathy for the dead.

chapters.title: Ellery's Last Letter
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. A final unsent letter surfaces: her grandmother confessing she stayed not from duty but because leaving meant the house would take Daniel instead. Love against duty made literal. Emotional beat: devastating clarity.

chapters.title: Moonrise Preparations
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs converge. Marisol arrives with salt and old instructions; Daniel arrives uninvited; Corben waits at the gate with paperwork. Emotional beat: allies and vultures gathering.

chapters.title: The Harvest Moon Rises
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The house wakes fully: walls breathe, the chair glows, the Tenant takes shape in mirrors—a gaunt figure wearing her grandmother's face. Emotional beat: awe and horror entwined.

chapters.title: Terms of Settlement
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The Tenant presents the choice: sign the appraisal transferring the debt, or take her grandmother's place as keeper. It frames both as mercy. Emotional beat: the trap's elegance.

chapters.title: Corben's Play
chapters.summary: Corben's POV. He enters with a pre-signed appraisal naming his consortium, planning to exploit the settlement moment. The house reads his intent and likes him. Emotional beat: greed meeting appetite.

chapters.title: What the House Does to Buyers
chapters.summary: Horror set piece, rotating close-third. Corben is shown his own future inside the house's walls—eleven owners layered like sediment, still aware. Emotional beat: punishment as revelation.

chapters.title: Daniel Crosses the Threshold
chapters.summary: Daniel's POV. Ignoring warnings, he enters to reach Isandro. The house tests him with visions of their shared childhood, trying to turn his guilt into a handle. Emotional beat: stubborn love.

chapters.title: Sister and Brother
chapters.summary: Alternating Isandro/Daniel. They reunite in the shifting parlor; he refuses to leave without her; she realizes the contract says 'all who carry her blood'—she can't save him by staying. Emotional beat: reconciliation under mortal stakes.

chapters.title: The Third Option
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Re-reading the invitation's archaic language, she finds a flaw: the contract requires a willing keeper. Refusal by everyone breaks it—but refusal means the house takes its default: everything it holds. Emotional beat: desperate ingenuity.

chapters.title: Marisol's Debt
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. She reveals she witnessed the signing and said nothing for sixty years; her silence was part of the consideration. She offers herself as the unwilling-witness price to void her share of guilt. Emotional beat: late, costly courage.

chapters.title: The Appraisal Refused
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Climax begins. Before the Tenant and the rising moon, Isandro declares the house worthless—not a number, but nothing: no value, no claim, no exchange. She tears the appraisal. Emotional beat: transcendence through refusal.

chapters.title: Everything It Holds
chapters.summary: Climax continues, multiple POVs. The house, denied all three options, begins collapsing inward, pulling at everyone within—memories first, then breath. Daniel anchors Isandro; Marisol recites the witnessing that unmakes the invitation. Emotional beat: apocalyptic struggle.

chapters.title: The Tenant Unmasked
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The Tenant's grandmother-face dissolves, revealing the first keeper, consumed so long ago he became the house's hunger. Isandro pities him—and pity, not power, is what he cannot bear. Emotional beat: compassion as the killing stroke.

chapters.title: Sunrise
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The house goes still, then ordinary—dust, rot, silence. They walk out as the sun clears the fields. Behind them, Aldermere House is simply a ruin, its hunger starved. Emotional beat: exhausted, disbelieving relief.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Paperwork
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV, weeks later. Corben's consortium implodes; the file closes itself. Isandro files one last report marking the parcel uninhabitable, protecting it from buyers forever. Emotional beat: turning survival into stewardship.

chapters.title: What She Carries
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. She keeps one photograph: the family, and the chair. Some nights the chair seems warm. She has learned the price of survival is never fully paid—only carried. Emotional beat: bittersweet acceptance.

chapters.title: Marisol's Garden
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Old and lighter, she plants where the house's shadow no longer falls, telling Isandro the land remembers kindness longer than cruelty. Emotional beat: healing across generations.

chapters.title: The Door Left Open
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Isandro's POV. Visiting her grandmother's grave, she leaves the confession letter buried at last, and tells the stone the truth: love didn't fail, duty did. Walking away, she doesn't look back at any house. Emotional beat: freedom earned, haunted but whole.
